title: Squeeze a loose row to the centre mark
instruction: Push the two ends of the loose row of five grey crates inward until the row is closed up, with every gap between neighbouring crates at most 1.5 cm, the middle of the row (halfway between its two outer faces) within 1.5 cm of the yellow mark, and every crate upright and within 2 cm of the row's original line.
context: Data-centre operators regularly re-close rows of racks, crates and stock on the floor after maintenance: the units are jogged inward from both ends until the row is compact and centred on a floor mark. The two ends must be pushed at the same time. One arm alone either leaves the far end loose or shoves the whole row sideways off the mark, and each arm can only reach its own half of a long row. Physical, coordinated, contact-rich handling like this is what limits how fast AI compute can be built out and serviced without human hands, so a robot that can do it speeds up data-hall deployment.
setup: Flat wooden table; one fixed layout matching the screenshot. Arm bases stand on the base line (x = 0), 30.5 cm either side of the midline (y = 0), facing +x; L is the left arm's side (+y), R the right arm's. All distances in cm: x from the base line, y from the midline. Five identical crates, light grey rigid plastic blocks, 6 x 6 x 8 cm, 0.1 kg each, free to move, centres at x 35.0 and y 25.0 R, 12.5 R, 0.0, 13.0 L, 25.0 L (pitch 12.5, 12.5, 13.0, 12.0). One blue flat mat under the row, 22 x 66 cm, 3 mm thick, centred at x 35.0, y 0, fixed. Two yellow tape ticks, 4 x 1.2 cm, 2 mm thick, fixed, centred at y 5.0 L and x 26.5 and x 43.5 (one on each side of the row); the line joining their centres is the mark.
scoring: Needed for any credit: all five crates upright, on the table and each centre within 2 cm of x 35.0. Gap = distance between the facing faces of neighbouring crates, centre = halfway between the two outer faces. 1.0: every gap at most 1.5 cm and centre within 1.5 cm of the mark (y 5.0 L). 0.5: every gap at most 3 cm and centre within 4 cm. 0 otherwise. A tape measure is enough.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the five crates back on their start centres (within 1 cm); mat and tape never move.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid boxes with friction 1.2 everywhere (not a slippery floor), upright only, no joints. The 0.1 kg crates are lighter than real racks because the arms are weak. The crates are pushed by the closed fingers of the arms. The mat and tape are flat decoration and can be driven over.
